messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a workspace preview in the console showing a run from another org. small repro: open /console/workspace/preview quickly after switching orgs and you can see rows from the previous org flash in the panel.

jess: ugh. any stack traces or logs?

kevin: pasted snippet from frontend logs: 
```
GET /api/console/prefetch?view=preview 200 34ms org_id=org-123 accept-affinity=true
cache_key=console:prefetch:preview:accept-affinity=true // NO org in key
```

kevin: Looks like prefetch cache key omits org scope when affinity flag is set.

sam: that matches a production incident I triaged last month (slowly creeping repros). affinity header was introduced in routing policy PR (edge side) and we added prefetch layer later — probably never updated key builder.

anya: if the cache key is global for that route, teams that rapidly switch org context can get other orgs' prefetched payloads. Renders and telemetry both affected.

jess: can we confirm whether the API layer enforces org scoping before returning prefetch data? or are we returning cache hits unchecked?

kevin: quick check: frontend calls /api/console/prefetch, gateway does auth and inserts X-Org header, but cache lookup happens at edge layer (before full auth) when accept-affinity=true to avoid cold miss. edge reads header from incoming request but the header isn't normalized so sometimes it's absent and it falls back to affinity-only key.

sam: repro plan: 1) enable detailed logs around cache key construction in canary region, 2) simulate rapid org switch with two test accounts, 3) assert no cross-org payloads returned.

anya: mitigation options: 1) make cache key include canonical org id ALWAYS (fastest), 2) flip accept-affinity flag off in prod (kill optimization), 3) short-term: add header validation guard: if X-Org missing => miss (safe).

jess: prefer 3 for immediate safety, then 1 as proper fix. 2 is disruptive for latency-sensitive routes.

kevin: +1 to 3. I can put up a tiny patch to edge to treat missing X-Org as miss and ship to canary now.

rollout-bot: Canary rollout started for service=edge-prefetch-handler by kevin (ver=2026.3.1) — 5% traffic.

sam: also worth adding a telemetry tag so we can track cross_org_cache_hits as a metric (count when cache_key lacked org but returned 200 with payload-not-empty). can be a short-lived metric for alerting.

anya: logging note: capture raw incoming headers, constructed cache_key, and user id/org id mapping for 5xx/debug windows only (PII caution). ops/security ok?

jess: ops: please rubber stamp logging as long as we redact user identifiers. security: @ops please confirm retention policy.

kevin: rolling patch to canary now. will post results in ~10m.

rollout-bot: Canary rollout 5% -> 20% (edge-prefetch-handler ver=2026.3.1).

kevin: canary looks clean at 20% — no more cross-org returns in repro script. promoting to 100% now.

rollout-bot: Rollout completed: edge-prefetch-handler ver=2026.3.1 at 100%.

jess: followups: 1) backfill test in integration suite for rapid org switch, 2) add unit to key builder to always include org id, 3) create small dashboard tile under console/telemetry for cross_org_cache_hits. assign owners?

anya: I'll take the dashboard. sam can add the integration test. kevin will follow up with the key-builder PR for next release.

sam: noted. also let's add a postmortem-lite doc in /incidents if we see any customer impact.

kevin: will draft a short incident note if we see any anomalous telemetry.

jess: thanks all. great catch and fast mitigation :thumbsup:
